label: canon-lvl-a19b17-tb
_why: THE TIE-BREAKER for canon_lvl_a19b17_n2 — run ONLY if alignment_check.mjs reports DIVERGENT on that pair (F114). Pool BOTH sessions in --arm when reading; the register takes the two closest intact runs on world GDP. THE MARGIN-COMPRESSION CAMPAIGN, BATCH 1 (ROADMAP step 9; user-ordered 2026-09-18 after the first human playtest: 'I really want to decrease margins across the board, in both early tiers (a bit) and the late tiers (a lot, otherwise both their margins and natural cost becomes exorbitant)' and then 'I would still prefer flatter but uniform (between industries) ladder'). Measured cause (ROADMAP step 8 P1): a rung's margin is (O x A^e) / (I x in0 x B^e / (1 - wp)) - 1, so r = A/B sets the ladder's SHAPE and in0 its LEVEL. The canon's r = 2.2/1.5 = 1.467 lands on a rung 0 sitting at about break-even, so the margin explodes 1.05 -> 1.54 -> 2.27 -> 3.33, i.e. +5% -> +55% -> +127% -> +233% at base prices against vanilla manufacturing's 23.1% realised. AND the level is NOT uniform: the scalar in0 multiplies vanilla's own recipes, whose margins differ wildly (glass +25%, textile +5%, steel -19%, arms +41%, the art academy +108%), so one r means a different thing in every industry and a uniform compression drives the thin chains negative while the fat ones stay fat. THIS BOOK FIXES BOTH HALVES: a new --in0-level 0.05 gives each industry its OWN era-0 lift so every industry's notional era-0 rung lands on +5%, and then A 1.9 / B 1.7 (r 1.118) compresses uniformly. RESULT, every industry identically: margins 5 / 17 / 31 / 47 by era, target_be 95 / 85 / 76 / 68 in all 56 rungs. It also moves three other playtest complaints at once: P5 (top-rung output 10.6x rung 0 -> 6.9x), P8 (an e3 costs 2,647 points against 4,115, so it builds in 64% of the time) and the hoard (F135: our doubled margins ARE the pool's inflow).

_delta: Against canon-c19-in12 (the incumbent and the canon): THREE coupled levers, which is deliberate - they are the two halves of one ladder redesign plus the cost that rides on A. (1) --in0-level 0.05 in place of --in0 1.2: a PER-INDUSTRY era-0 lift (0.93 steel ... 1.21 textile ... 1.43 glass ... 1.61 arms ... 2.14 automotive ... 2.38 art academy) so every industry's notional era-0 margin is +5%. (2) A 1.9 / B 1.7 in place of 2.2 / 1.5: r 1.118 against 1.467. (3) cost anchor x 1.64^era in place of 1.9^era, which holds capital per unit of output at the canon's own ratio (C/A = 0.864) so only the MARGIN moves, not the incentive to climb. Unchanged: ai_value 1000 x 3^era, divisor 0.000125, the section 10.75 defines, the 24-month research bar, the era rule, the 1836 start rules. ⚠ Attribution is limited by construction: a reading cannot be split between the levelling and the compression. That is accepted - the user ordered the pair.

_predictions.gdp: world GDP 0.85-1.10x the vanilla per-run median at the end state (the incumbent 1.10). Lower output per level (A 1.9 against 2.2) needs more levels for the same product, so the GDP lines should soften; the cheaper frontier (cost 64% of the canon's at e3) pushes the other way. A stall below 0.75 is the failure mode to watch and would most likely start in the 1860s-1890s, not at 1836.
_predictions.workers: productive workers per capita 0.72-0.90x world and 0.80-0.95 on the pool (the incumbent 0.69 / 0.68). Lower A means more levels and more workers - F129 measured exactly this on the A axis (0.85-0.91 world) and it was judged an overshoot then; the widened pool W aim (section 10.85, 0.6-0.95) is what makes it affordable now. Shortlist unemployment incl. peasants 25-40% (the incumbent 40-45%).
_predictions.hoard: ⭐ THE KEY READING. World pools 0.20-0.45 of GDP at 1935 and the pool's H 1.0-2.5x vanilla (the incumbent 0.42-0.91 and 4.17x). The margin ladder IS the pool's inflow (F135: our realised margins 26/31/47/46% against vanilla manufacturing's 23.1%), and this book roughly halves the base-price margins above era 0, so the hoard should fall WITHOUT the eager defines. If it falls and world GDP does not, F135's diagnosis is confirmed and the A/B gap is the hoard's real lever.
_predictions.obsolescence: realised margins by era roughly 15 / 20 / 28 / 30% at 1935 (the incumbent 26 / 31 / 47 / 46) - the LADDER's shape should survive even though its level halves, because r > 1 still. Rung 0 40-55% staffed; T0 0.6-1.0x the 1900s; below-best 28-38%. ⚠ A flatter ladder is a WEAKER obsolescence signal: if T0 rises or the frontier stops out-earning the old rung, the compression has gone too far and r must come back up.
_predictions.prices: PI 0.82-0.92 and PP 0.78-0.90 (the incumbent 0.84 / 0.83). Cheaper frontier output per level means less glut per level, so the tiered prices may sit slightly HIGHER than the incumbent's - the price decline is bought by volume, and this book has less volume per level.
_predictions.anchor_1836: ⚠⚠ THE OTHER KEY RISK. Levelling removes the cushion the fat industries had at 1836: glass, tooling and paper drop from +25% to +5% at base, arms from +41%, the art academy from +108%. F137 shows the canon's own 1836 prices are already BELOW base in exactly the industries with the most converted starting capacity (British tools 21% of base, clothes 56%), so those buildings start thinner than ever. WATCH the 1836-1845 anchor line and the 1840/1850 dumps for an early collapse; the register's HARD anchor test (world GDP outside vanilla's 90% CI +/-10% in more than two years) is the tripwire.
_predictions.perf: row P total within +/-10% of the vanilla median play time; the resume feeder handles a CTD (L32).

_register: Read under THE CRITERIA REGISTER (section 10.83, as amended by 10.83.7 and 10.85 - the shortlist aims are pool W 0.6-0.95 and pool GDP 1.1-1.9, world U* is out of the loss, sigma is fixed). In the register's terms: world GDP 0.85-1.10 (aim 1.0), pool GDP 1.0-1.7 (aim 1.1-1.9), pool W 0.80-0.95 (at the widened aim's top), pool U* 1.0-1.6 (⚠ below the >= 2 aim, which now CONTRADICTS pool W's - unruled, section 10.85), pool H 1.0-2.5x (aim < 1; the incumbent 4.17), world H 0.5-1.5x, PI 0.82-0.92, PP 0.78-0.90, T0/rest 0.03-0.06, T3/rest 0.30-0.40. EXPECTED LOSS 6-14 against the incumbent's 7.9 under the amended form - i.e. it is NOT expected to win on the loss alone, and that is not the point: the hoard term is the incumbent's second-largest and this is the first book that attacks its INFLOW rather than its outflow. THE ADOPT RULE, re-based (section 10.83.7, the statistics are DIRECTIONAL): a HARD break in any run ends the config; otherwise the candidate replaces the incumbent when it beats the loss AND the lever's direction is understood AND it adds no hard break - the judgement is the user's, and a loss gap under ~13 is inside the noise (sigma of one run's loss 6.6).
